newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber finishes lower on Tokyo drop.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber finishes lower on Tokyo drop.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were lower at the close after moving in tight ranges because of lack of overseas demand but dealers said they expect the long-term trend to remain steady due to the underlying firm sentiment.
"The market eased because of falls in Tokyo," a dealer said.
Dealers said news of a U.S. missile attack on Iraq has no impact on the market which also lacks keen consumer demand.
There were only light enquiries from South Korea and Taiwan but dealers were unaware of any deals being done.
Players are still positive of the near-term trend because of expectation of slow supplies following the wet weather.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set market indicator price for new trading month October RSS1 buyer at 331.50 cents ($1.33) a kg, down a cent from Monday while October SMR 20 buyer eased half a cent to 317.50.
Traders quoted SMR10 sellers at 319 cents, SMR CV at 380 to 382, SMR L at 360 and drum latex FOB at 250-253.
The INRO five-day average was 250.36 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 2 from 249.00 on August 30. The daily indicator was 252.69 against 250.94.
